tasks.title: Calibrating BATT_VOLT_MULT
tasks.statement: `BATT_VOLT_MULT` is set to **{m}**. Mission Planner shows **{vr} V**, and a multimeter on the battery balance lead shows **{vm} V**. What new value of `BATT_VOLT_MULT` do you write?
tasks.solution: The firmware computes V = (V_pin − BATT_VLT_OFFSET) · BATT_VOLT_MULT, so the reading is directly proportional to the multiplier. New multiplier = old · V_multimeter / V_GCS. If the GCS reads low, the multiplier goes up.

tasks.title: BATT_AMP_PERVLT from the charger
tasks.statement: `BATT_AMP_PERVLT` is set to **{k} A/V**. After a flight the flight controller counted **{mfc} mAh**, and the charger put **{mch} mAh** back into the battery (charged to the same voltage as before the flight; the zero offset is already calibrated). What is the new value of `BATT_AMP_PERVLT`?
tasks.solution: I = (V_pin − BATT_AMP_OFFSET) · BATT_AMP_PERVLT, and mAh is the integral of current, so the capacity error equals the scale error. New = old · mAh_charger / mAh_flight_controller. The charger is the more honest reference: it measures what actually left the battery (less a charging efficiency correction of ~2–5 %).

tasks.title: BATT_AMP_OFFSET from the zero reading
tasks.statement: The board is powered over USB, the main battery is disconnected, and the current through the sensor is zero. With `BATT_AMP_PERVLT` = **{k} A/V** and `BATT_AMP_OFFSET` = **{o} V** the GCS shows **{i0} A**. What new value of `BATT_AMP_OFFSET` (V) zeroes the reading?
tasks.solution: The sensor zero: I₀ = (V_pin − o) · k, so V_pin = o + I₀/k. That voltage is the new offset. The offset is calibrated first; otherwise a scale fitted at one current point is wrong at every other point.

tasks.title: Hover PWM from T/W
tasks.statement: The copter has a thrust-to-weight ratio of **{tw}** (maximum thrust is at `MOT_SPIN_MAX` = 0.95), `MOT_THST_EXPO` = **{e}**, `MOT_SPIN_MIN` = **{smin}**, `MOT_PWM_MIN/MAX` = 1000/2000 µs, and voltage compensation is off. Taking `MOT_THST_HOVER` = 1/(T/W), find the PWM at the motor output in a hover (µs).
tasks.solution: Hover thrust t = 1/(T/W). The AP_Motors linearization (Thrust_Linearization): r = ((e−1) + √((1−e)² + 4·e·t)) / (2e), the inverse of T = (1−e)·r + e·r². Output: actuator = SPIN_MIN + (SPIN_MAX − SPIN_MIN)·r, PWM = PWM_MIN + actuator·(PWM_MAX − PWM_MIN). Example: T/W 3, e 0.65, SPIN_MIN 0.15 → t 0.333, r 0.496, PWM ≈ 1547 µs.
